factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial review: Gross profit €13,535k (2025) vs €16,770k (2024); Gross margin 6.5% (2025) vs 7.5% (2024).

factual_claims.claim: Operating profit decreased 30% to €5.65 million, reducing the operating margin to 2.7% from 3.6%, below the group’s target of consistently exceeding 3%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial review: Operating profit €5,651k (2025) vs €8,061k (2024) (~30% decrease); Operating margin 2.7% (2025) vs 3.6% (2024). Directors' report states financial target: Operating margin consistently above 3%.

factual_claims.claim: EBITDA fell to €8.25 million from €11.0 million, with the EBITDA margin declining to 4.0% from 4.9%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial review: EBITDA €8,250k (2025) vs €11,025k (2024); EBITDA margin 4.0% (2025) vs 4.9% (2024).

factual_claims.claim: Administrative expenses decreased 14% to €6.8 million, largely because weaker performance resulted in lower performance-based pay, but this reduction did not offset the decline in gross profit.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 11: Administrative expenses €6,814k (2025) vs €7,878k (2024) (~14% decrease). People section explains decrease due to lower staff costs from weaker performance and reduced performance-based pay liability.

factual_claims.claim: Net profit fell to €2.55 million from €5.17 million, while profit attributable to Nordecon’s owners declined to €1.44 million from €3.83 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial review: Net profit €2,545k (2025) vs €5,165k (2024). Consolidated statement of comprehensive income: Profit attributable to owners of parent €1,439k (2025) vs €3,827k (2024).

factual_claims.claim: Earnings per share decreased to €0.05 from €0.12.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 7: Basic earnings per share €0.05 (2025) vs €0.12 (2024).

factual_claims.claim: Net finance costs increased to €3.0 million from €2.3 million, primarily because the Ukrainian hryvnia weakened approximately 12% against the euro, producing a €750 thousand foreign-exchange loss on loans to Ukrainian subsidiaries, compared with €258 thousand in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 13: Total finance costs €3,464k (2025) vs €3,011k (2024). Foreign exchange loss €750k (2025) vs €258k (2024). Financial risks section states hryvnia weakened ~12% against euro in 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Credit losses also increased to €354 thousand from €20 thousand.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial risks section: Credit losses for the year amounted to €354k (2025) vs €20k (2024).

factual_claims.claim: The Estonian construction market stabilised, with activity improving modestly in the second half of the year, while construction prices rose 1.5%, mainly because of higher material prices.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Key figures and Operations in Estonia: Construction market stabilised with slight increase in H2; construction price index increased 1.5% in 2025 primarily due to material price upward trend.

factual_claims.claim: Competition remained intense, public investment in buildings declined, and underfunding continued to constrain road construction.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operations in Estonia and Description of main risks: Competition remains fierce; public investment in buildings sector decreased; underfunding of road construction continues.

factual_claims.claim: Against this backdrop, new contracts secured increased to €235.0 million from €181.4 million, lifting the order book 30% to €273.1 million at year-end.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section: New contracts secured €234,994k (2025) vs €181,437k (2024); order book €273,060k (2025) vs €209,489k (2024) represents ~30% increase.

factual_claims.claim: Infrastructure accounted for 42% of the backlog, up from 18%, supported by major Rail Baltica and road-construction contracts, while the Buildings backlog declined 7%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section: Infrastructure segment share of order book 42% (2025) vs 18% (2024); Buildings segment share 58% (2025) vs 82% (2024) represents ~7% decrease. Mentions Rail Baltica and road construction contracts as key drivers.

factual_claims.claim: Management expects business volumes to increase in 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section concluding paragraph: Based on order book size and market outlook, management expects business volumes to increase in 2026.

factual_claims.claim: Operating cash inflow was €1.2 million, slightly above 2024, but investing and financing outflows resulted in a €2.8 million net cash reduction.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash flow statement: Net cash from operating activities €1,204k (2025) vs €1,075k (2024); Net cash flow €(2,757k) (2025). The summary states investing and financing outflows caused the net reduction.

factual_claims.claim: Year-end cash declined to €5.3 million from €8.2 million, and the current ratio remained weak at 0.93.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash and cash equivalents: €5,266k (2025) vs €8,195k (2024). Liquidity risk section: Current ratio 0.93 (2025) described as weak.

factual_claims.claim: No dividends were paid in 2025.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash flow from financing activities: Dividends paid €0 (2025) vs €1,347k (2024). Directors' report confirms no dividends were paid.
